mainTopic: Using blood gathered from the floor of the עזרה according to רבי יהודה, and which intentions can make a קרבן פיגול.
overview: The amud opens with רבי יהודה's answer to the חכמים: he allows blood gathered from the floor only when it was first caught in a כלי and spilled afterward. The גמרא explains that we can assume this, because כהנים are careful but work fast. It then asks about דם התמצית mixed into the floor-blood. It first answers that רבי יהודה calls it real blood, but רבי אלעזר shows that even he agrees it does not bring כפרה. So the גמרא answers instead that, for רבי יהודה, blood does not cancel out blood. The ברייתא continues: the חכמים explain that the drain of the עזרה was plugged to honor the כהנים, who walked in blood. The גמרא then works through two problems with that picture, חציצה and dirty clothes, and ends with the כהנים walking on raised platforms. A new משנה teaches which improper intentions do not ruin a קרבן: unusual parts, less than a כזית, eating and burning together, non-meat parts, a fetus, eggs and milk. The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's one-way rule of פיגול. It begins to test a ברייתא that seems to support him, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits his ruling to blood first caught in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers the חכמים: he only allowed spilled blood when it had first been received in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: I too only said this when the blood had been received in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה is replying to the חכמים, who argued that blood gathered from the floor was never received in a כלי. He says he agrees: he only allows it when it was first caught in a כלי and spilled afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים thought רבי יהודה allowed blood that went straight from the neck to the floor. He clarifies that his case is narrower. The blood already had a proper קבלה in a כלי, and only spilled after that.

keyTerms.meaning: I too (I agree with you on this point)
a vessel (here, the sacred cup for collecting blood)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying blood straight from the floor is valid. He is only talking about blood that was first caught in a כלי and then spilled.

phrases.english: I too did not say it
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is answering the חכמים from the ברייתא on the previous page.

phrases.english: except when it was received in a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁנִּתְקַבֵּל בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' objection from the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים thought רבי יהודה allowed blood that never went into a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה only allows blood that was received in a כלי first and spilled afterward.

steps.title: How can רבי יהודה know the blood was caught first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can know that the spilled blood had already been received in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he himself, how does he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about רבי יהודה's ruling. Once blood is on the floor, how can anyone tell it was caught in a כלי first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's ruling depends on a fact that seems impossible to check. The blood on the floor looks the same whether it spilled from the neck or from the כלי. The גמרא wants to know what lets him assume the good case.

phrases.english: But he himself, from where does he know?
phrases.notes: "He" means רבי יהודה, or whoever is relying on his ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the case defined in step 1 could ever be known.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How it can be known that blood on the floor was first received in a כלי.

steps.title: Priests are careful but quick, so blood spills from the cup
steps.stepSummary: כהנים are careful and surely caught the blood, but they work fast, so blood spills from the כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Priests are diligent, and they work quickly, and the blood spills.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we can assume the blood was caught in a כלי. כהנים are careful to catch all the blood, and because they work fast, some spills out of the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facts about כהנים make the answer work. Because they are careful, we assume the blood went into the כלי. Because they are fast, it is normal for blood to splash out of the כלי afterward.

phrases.english: Priests are diligent,
phrases.notes: So we can trust they caught the blood in the כלי.

phrases.english: and they work quickly, and it spills.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We assume the blood was caught, since כהנים are careful. The spill came from the כלי because they work fast.

steps.title: The floor blood is mixed with weaker blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the blood on the floor is mixed with דם התמצית, which should make it unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't blood of exudate mixed in with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רבי יהודה's view. Even if the blood came from the כלי, on the floor it gets mixed with דם התמצית, the slow blood that drips out after the main flow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דם התמצית is not the main lifeblood that pours out at שחיטה. If it mixes into the gathered blood, the priest might be sprinkling unfit blood. That seems to undo רבי יהודה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: blood of exudate (the slow drip that comes out after the main flow)

phrases.english: But isn't blood of exudate mixed in with it!
phrases.notes: דם התמצית is the slow dripping blood that comes out after the main gush, and it lands on the floor too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the knowledge problem is solved, the גמרא attacks the quality of the gathered blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that gathered floor blood is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The floor blood is mixed with דם התמצית, which is not proper blood for sprinkling.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds exudate blood counts as blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own view that דם התמצית is called real blood, so the mixture is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, for he says: blood of exudate is called blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה is consistent with his own opinion elsewhere. For him, דם התמצית counts as real blood, so mixing it in does not ruin anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed דם התמצית is weaker blood. The גמרא says רבי יהודה does not accept that. If it is full blood for him, the mixture is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: is called blood (counts as real blood)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
for he says: blood of exudate is called blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the author's known opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דם התמצית is weaker blood and spoils the mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, דם התמצית is real blood, so the mixture is valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה gives exudate blood כרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that for the תנא קמא eating דם התמצית is a plain prohibition, while for רבי יהודה it carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Blood of exudate is under a prohibition. רבי יהודה says: it carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה treats דם התמצית as real blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives only an אזהרה, a plain prohibition, for eating דם התמצית. That is lighter than eating lifeblood. רבי יהודה gives כרת, the same punishment as for full blood, which shows he sees it as real blood.

keyTerms.meaning: spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating real blood

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, דם התמצית is real blood: eating it brings כרת. That is why he is not bothered by it mixing into the gathered floor blood.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Blood of exudate is under a prohibition.
phrases.notes: Eating it is forbidden, but it does not carry the heavier punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it carries karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 5 about רבי יהודה's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה considers דם התמצית real blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה gives כרת for eating דם התמצית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says exudate blood still does not atone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אלעזר says even רבי יהודה agrees that דם התמצית does not bring כפרה, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: רבי יהודה agrees regarding atonement that it does not atone, as it says: 'For the blood is the soul'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 5. רבי אלעזר says that for כפרה on the מזבח, even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not work. The next step spells out what the פסוק teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא showed that רבי יהודה treats דם התמצית as blood for eating. Sprinkling on the מזבח is about כפרה, and here even he agrees it does not count. So the problem of the mixed-in blood seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't (he) say? An opening for a challenge
as it is said (introducing a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: There is no contradiction in רבי יהודה's view. He treats דם התמצית as blood for the איסור of eating, but not for כפרה. The two areas follow different rules.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding atonement
that it does not atone,
as it is said: "For the blood is the soul" –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְעִנְיַן כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in steps 5-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יהודה treats דם התמצית as real blood, so the mixture is fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For כפרה even רבי יהודה agrees דם התמצית does not count, so the mixture should still make the sprinkling unfit.

steps.title: Only blood that carries out the life counts as blood
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק cited by רבי אלעזר teaches that only blood the life leaves with is called blood, so דם התמצית should be unfit even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that the life goes out with is called 'blood.' Blood that the life does not go out with is not called 'blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in step 7 by spelling out what the פסוק teaches. Blood that the life does not leave with, like דם התמצית, does not count as 'blood' for bringing כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that רבי יהודה calls דם התמצית real blood for the איסור of eating it. This פסוק shows that for כפרה on the מזבח, only the blood the animal dies with counts. So step 5's answer seems to fail, because the floor-blood mixture should still be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: The life goes out with it; the first gush of blood that kills the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. Calling דם התמצית 'blood' for the איסור of eating it is one thing. Calling it 'blood' for bringing כפרה on the מזבח is a different thing.

phrases.english: Blood that the life goes out with
phrases.notes: This is the lesson of the פסוק that רבי אלעזר quoted in step 7: the blood that spurts out at the slaughter.

phrases.english: is called 'blood';
blood that the life does not go out with
is not called 'blood'!

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּם שֶׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ יוֹצְאָה בּוֹ קָרוּי דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 7 by spelling out what the פסוק teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 5, that רבי יהודה allows the mixture because he calls דם התמצית real blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For כפרה, the פסוק excludes blood the life does not leave with. So even רבי יהודה must treat דם התמצית as unfit, and the mixture should be unfit.

steps.title: Blood does not cancel out blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's real reason is that blood cannot nullify other blood, so the good blood in the mixture stays usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה is following his own view, because he says: blood does not cancel out blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the reason from step 5 and gives a new one. רבי יהודה holds that when blood is mixed with blood, the good blood is not 'lost' in the mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now agree that דם התמצית itself cannot bring כפרה. But the כשר blood that spilled from the כלי is still in the mixture, and the דם התמצית does not cancel it out. So the whole mixture may be put on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood does not cancel out (nullify) blood
Following his own reasoning, a view he holds elsewhere
Nullification; when a small amount gets 'lost' in a larger mixture

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the basis of רבי יהודה's ruling. The mixture is usable because of a rule about mixtures, not because of the status of דם התמצית itself.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning,
for he says: blood does not cancel out blood.
phrases.notes: So the good blood in the mixture is not 'lost' in the דם התמצית, and the whole mixture can be used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 7–8 by replacing step 5's reason with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reason with a different principle of רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה allowed the mixture because he treats דם התמצית as real blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: He allows it because blood cannot nullify blood, so the כשר blood in the mixture stays fit.

steps.title: Why plug the drain of the עזרה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה challenges the חכמים, asking why the drain of the עזרה was plugged if the floor-blood cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to them: According to your view, why do they plug the drain of the עזרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes more of it. רבי יהודה challenges the חכמים, who say the blood on the floor may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the floor-blood is useless, there is no reason to keep it from draining away. Plugging the drain makes sense only if the blood is being saved so the כהנים can collect it. רבי יהודה uses this practice as support for his view.

keyTerms.meaning: They plug up (a drain or opening)
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the חכמים, the תנא קמא of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: According to your words,
why do they plug up the courtyard?
phrases.notes: He means the drain in the floor of the courtyard, so the blood would not run out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא and quotes רבי יהודה's argument against the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that blood gathered from the floor may not be used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plugging the drain only makes sense if the blood is being kept to be used, so the practice suggests floor-blood is usable.

steps.title: It is an honor for the כהנים to walk in blood
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the drain was plugged to honor the כהנים, letting them walk in blood up to their ankles.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is a praise for the sons of אהרן that they walk in blood up to their ankles.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה's question. The drain was not plugged to save the blood for use but to give honor to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give the plugged drain a different reason, so it no longer proves that floor-blood can be used. Walking in deep blood shows how much עבודה the כהנים are doing. רבי יהודה's proof is pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of אהרן, the כהנים
Their joints; here understood as their ankles

phrases.english: They said to him:
It is a praise for the sons of Aaron
that they should walk in blood up to their ankles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שֶׁבַח הוּא לִבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה's question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The drain was plugged to honor the כהנים, not to save the blood for use.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the practice a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plugging the drain shows the floor-blood was being saved for use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drain was plugged to honor the כהנים, so it proves nothing about using the floor-blood.

steps.title: Isn't the blood a blocking layer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: blood between the כהנים' feet and the floor should be a חציצה and ruin the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But blood is a blocking layer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the answer of the חכמים. If the כהנים stand in blood, it seems to come between their feet and the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן must stand directly on the floor of the עזרה when he does the עבודה. Anything in between counts as a חציצה and makes the עבודה פסול. So walking in blood should be a problem, not an honor.

keyTerms.meaning: A blocking layer between two things that must touch directly

phrases.english: But the blood is a blocking layer!
phrases.notes: It would come between the כהן's feet and the floor, which must touch directly during the עבודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהנים walked in blood during the עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood under the feet seems to separate the כהן from the floor, which should make his עבודה פסול.

steps.title: Wet blood does not block
steps.stepSummary: The blood is wet, and a source teaches that wet substances like blood, ink, honey and milk do not count as a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is wet, so it is not a blocking layer. As we learned: blood, ink, honey and milk block when they are dry, but when they are wet they do not block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wet blood is not a חציצה. It brings a source to show that wet liquids do not block, only dry ones do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts as a blocking layer only when it has dried and sticks as a separate layer. Fresh, wet blood is not treated that way. So the כהנים may stand in the blood and their עבודה is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: They block; they form a חציצה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה lets floor-blood be used because blood does not cancel out blood. The חכמים say the drain was plugged only to honor the כהנים, and the wet blood is not a חציצה.

phrases.english: It is wet, and it is not a blocking layer.
As we learned:
Blood, ink, honey, and milk –
when dry, they block;
when wet, they do not block.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַח הוּא, וְלָא הָוֵי חֲצִיצָה. דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and brings a source to back up the answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction: wet versus dry, backed by a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any blood under the feet would be a חציצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only dried substances block; wet blood does not, so the עבודה is כשר.

steps.title: Walking in blood would dirty the כהנים' clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the כהנים walked in blood, their clothes would get dirty. A משנה teaches that a כהן who serves in dirty clothes has an invalid עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But their clothes would get dirty! And we learned: if his clothes were dirty and he served, his service is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the idea that the כהנים walked in blood up to their ankles: their clothes would get soiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 solved the חציצה problem for their feet. Now the גמרא points to a different problem, the clothing. A source says that serving in soiled בגדי כהונה makes the עבודה invalid, so walking in blood seems to ruin the service.

phrases.english: But their clothes get dirty!
And we learned:
If his clothes were soiled and he served,
his service is invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חציצה problem is solved, a new problem is raised about the same picture of כהנים walking in blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that the כהנים walked in blood up to their ankles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Walking in blood soils the clothes, and soiled clothes make the עבודה invalid.

steps.title: They could not lift their clothes up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer, that the כהנים held their clothes up. A כהן's garment must fit him exactly, no shorter and no longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they lifted their clothes up, but it was taught: 'his garment (מדו)' means according to his measure, not too short and not too long!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easy way out, that the כהנים lifted their clothes, and immediately shows why that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word מדו as 'his measure': a כהן's garment must be exactly his size. Lifting the garment would make it effectively too short, so the easy answer fails and the קשיא from step 14 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: And if you say that they lifted them up,
but it was taught: 'his garment' means according to his measure,
that it should not be too short and not too long!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects in advance a possible answer to the קשיא of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the כהנים lifted their garments to keep them clean
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A כהן's garment must be exactly his length, and lifting it changes that.

steps.title: They walked in blood only while carrying limbs to the ramp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כהנים walked in the blood only while carrying limbs to the כבש, which it assumes is not a real עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was while carrying the limbs to the ramp, which is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about dirty clothes: the walking in blood happened only during a task that does not count as an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that dirty clothes invalidate applies only to a real עבודה. If the כהנים walked in the blood only while carrying limbs to the כבש, then dirty clothes at that moment do no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: the ramp leading up to the מזבח
it is not a Temple service

phrases.english: During the carrying of limbs to the ramp,
which is not a service.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהוֹלָכַת אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ, דְּלָאו עֲבוֹדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 14-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a moment that is not an עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Walking in the blood would ruin an עבודה because the clothes get dirty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The walking took place only while carrying limbs, which this answer assumes is not an עבודה.

steps.title: Carrying limbs is a real service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that carrying the limbs to the כבש is an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not a service?! But it was taught: 'And the כהן shall bring it all' refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 16 by showing that carrying limbs does count as an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the words 'והקריב הכהן את הכל' that carrying the limbs to the כבש is part of the עבודה. If so, dirty clothes during that carrying would ruin it, and the answer of step 16 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is not?! (expresses surprise at a claim)
and he shall bring near / offer

phrases.english: And it is not?!
But it was taught: 'And the priest shall bring it all':
this is the carrying of limbs to the ramp!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that carrying limbs to the כבש is not an עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives from a פסוק that carrying limbs is an עבודה.

steps.title: They walked in blood only while carrying wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the כהנים walked in the blood only while carrying wood to the מערכה, which really is not an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was while carrying wood to the arrangement on the altar, which is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its first answer with a better one, choosing a task that truly is not an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same: dirty clothes do not matter during a task that is not an עבודה. Only the example changes, from carrying limbs, which is an עבודה, to carrying wood for the fire, which is not.

keyTerms.meaning: the arranged wood pile on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather, during the carrying of wood to the arrangement on the altar,
which is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a different task that is not an עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The walking happened while carrying limbs, which turned out to be an עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The walking happened while carrying wood, which is not an עבודה.

steps.title: How did they reach the real services?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the floor was full of blood, how did the כהנים get to the real עבודות without dirtying their clothes?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the service, how did they walk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up question. It is setting up the next step, which explains how the כהנים walked to the real services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 covered only the wood-carrying. The real עבודות still had to be done in that same blood-filled עזרה, so the גמרא asks how the כהנים got there without soiling their clothes.

phrases.english: And for the service, how did they walk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question on the answer of step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the כהנים walked to real עבודות without dirtying their clothes

steps.title: They walked on raised platforms
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים walked on raised platforms, so the blood on the floor did not touch their clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They walked on platforms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for real עבודות, the כהנים walked on raised platforms above the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the discussion. The blood was on the floor, which honored the כהנים, but they only stepped into it while carrying wood. For real עבודות they walked on platforms, so their clothes stayed clean.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים walked in the blood only while carrying wood, which is not an עבודה. For real עבודות they walked on raised platforms, so their clothes were never soiled during a service.

phrases.english: They walked on platforms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They walked on raised platforms above the blood.

steps.title: Intending to eat or burn the wrong part
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if someone slaughters a קרבן intending to eat a part that is not normally eaten, or to burn a part that is not normally burned (beyond its time or outside its place), the קרבן is still valid. רבי אליעזר says it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters an offering intending to eat something that is not normally eaten, or to burn something that is not normally burned, the offering is valid. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a bad intention only ruins a קרבן when it matches the normal use of that part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intention to eat or burn a קרבן beyond its time or outside its place usually ruins it. Here the תנא קמא says the intention does not count when it does not fit how that part is normally used, like planning to eat the parts that go on the מזבח. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says even this kind of intention ruins the קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say it, but the intention here is to eat or burn beyond the proper time or outside the proper place. It is not about eating or burning normally.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters the offering
intending to eat something that is not normally eaten,
phrases.notes: Read this as planning to eat it after its time or outside its place, the kind of intention that usually ruins a קרבן.

phrases.english: or to burn something that is not normally burned,
it is valid. And Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An improper intention about a part used in an unusual way does not ruin the קרבן, according to the תנא קמא. רבי אליעזר disagrees.

steps.title: Less than a כזית, and eating and burning do not combine
steps.stepSummary: An improper intention about less than a כזית does not ruin a קרבן. Half a כזית to eat plus half a כזית to burn also does not add up to a full measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: To eat something normally eaten, or burn something normally burned, but less than an olive-bulk: it is valid. To eat half an olive-bulk and burn half an olive-bulk: it is valid, since eating and burning do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more cases where a bad intention does not ruin the קרבן: the amount is too small, or two different half-amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the intention fits the part's normal use, it must be about at least a כזית. Two half-measures do not join together because eating and burning are different actions.
steps.whatToRemember: An improper intention ruins a קרבן only if it fits the part's normal use and covers at least a כזית of one kind of action. Eating and burning do not join together.

phrases.english: To eat something that is normally eaten,
or to burn something that is normally burned,
less than an olive-bulk: it is valid.
To eat half an olive-bulk
and to burn half an olive-bulk: it is valid,
since eating and burning do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל, וּלְהַקְטִיר דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לְהַקְטִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention about less than a כזית does not ruin the קרבן, and half a כזית of eating plus half a כזית of burning do not combine.

steps.title: Intention to eat hide, bones, horns and similar parts does not ruin the offering
steps.stepSummary: If someone slaughters a קרבן intending to eat a כזית of hide, gravy, spices, אלל, bones, tendons, horns or hooves beyond its time or outside its place, the קרבן stays valid. No one is punished for these parts because of פיגול, נותר or טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters an offering intending to eat an olive-size from the hide, the gravy, the spices, the neck tendon, the bones, the tendons, the horns or the hooves, beyond its time or outside its place: the offering is valid, and there is no liability for these parts because of פיגול, נותר or eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists parts of an animal that do not count as real meat of the קרבן, so a wrong intention about them changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An improper intention only works on parts that are normally eaten as the קרבן's meat. Hide, bones, horns and the like are not real meat, so planning to eat them at the wrong time or place does nothing. The same reason explains why eating them brings no punishment for פיגול, נותר or טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide or skin of the animal
Gravy or juice from cooking the meat
Spices and bits that collect at the bottom of the pot
A tough neck tendon that is not really meat
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time

phrases.english: One who slaughters the offering
intending to eat an olive-size from the hide,
or from the gravy, or from the spices,
or from the neck tendon, or from the bones,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַגִּידִין, וּמִן הַקְּרָנַיִם, וּמִן הַטְּלָפַיִם –
phrases.english: or from the tendons, or from the horns, or from the hooves –
beyond its time or outside its place;
it is valid,
and one is not liable for them
because of פיגול, נותר, or eating while impure.
phrases.notes: Each of these three would normally bring כרת. Here none applies, because these parts are not real meat of the קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לֶאֱכוֹל כְּזַיִת מִן הָעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of intentions that do not ruin a קרבן, now naming specific non-meat parts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intention about non-meat parts such as hide, bones, horns and hooves does not ruin the קרבן, and eating them brings no punishment for פיגול, נותר or טמא.

steps.title: Intention about a fetus, a placenta or eggs does not make the offering פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering a sacred animal intending to eat its fetus or placenta outside does not make it פיגול. Doing מליקה on doves intending to eat their eggs outside also does not make it פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters sacred animals intending to eat the fetus or the placenta outside has not made it פיגול. One who does מליקה on doves intending to eat their eggs outside has not made it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds things found inside the animal or bird and says that a wrong intention about them does not ruin the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus, a placenta and eggs are not counted as part of the animal's or bird's own body. So intending to eat them at the wrong time or place is like intending about something separate, and the קרבן is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus inside the mother animal
The way a bird קרבן is killed: the כהן cuts the back of the neck with his fingernail

phrases.english: One who slaughters sacred animals
intending to eat the fetus or the placenta outside –
has not made it פיגול.
One who does מליקה on doves
intending to eat their eggs outside –
has not made it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁלִיל אוֹ שִׁילְיָא בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from non-meat parts of the animal to things inside it that are not part of its body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intention about a fetus, a placenta or eggs does not make an animal or bird קרבן פיגול.

steps.title: No punishment for the milk of sacred animals or the eggs of doves
steps.stepSummary: The milk of sacred animals and the eggs of doves bring no punishment for פיגול, נותר or eating while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The milk of sacred animals and the eggs of doves: one is not liable for them because of פיגול, נותר, or eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes the list. Milk and eggs are not part of the קרבן's body, so the punishments for eating a קרבן wrongly do not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said that intending about eggs does not ruin the קרבן. This step adds that actually eating milk or eggs in a forbidden way brings no כרת either, because they are not counted as the קרבן itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure, here meaning eating a קרבן while impure

steps.confusionAlert: Here חֲלֵב, said with a tzeirei, means MILK. It is not חֵלֶב, the forbidden fat. Same letters, different word.
steps.whatToRemember: Only the real body and meat of the קרבן can become פיגול. Hide, bones, horns, a fetus, a placenta, eggs and milk are all outside that.

phrases.english: The milk of sacred animals and the eggs of doves –
one is not liable for them
because of פיגול, נותר, or eating while impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the egg case: eating these items in a forbidden way also brings no punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no liability for פיגול, נותר or טמא for the milk of sacred animals or for doves' eggs.

steps.title: When the offering becomes פיגול, its fetus does too, but not the other way around
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says: if the קרבן itself is made פיגול, its fetus becomes פיגול as well. If the wrong intention was only about the fetus, the קרבן does not become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: If he made פיגול with the offering, the fetus becomes פיגול. If he did it with the fetus, the offering does not become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a rule from רבי אלעזר that adds to the משנה's case of the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that intending about the fetus does not ruin the קרבן. רבי אלעזר adds the other direction: when the mother becomes פיגול, the fetus inside it is pulled along and becomes פיגול too. The main item carries the side item, but the side item cannot carry the main one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a one-way rule: the main part of the קרבן passes its status to a lesser part, but not the other way.

phrases.english: Gemara: רבי אלעזר says:
If he made פיגול with the offering, the fetus becomes פיגול.
With the fetus, the offering does not become פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: פִּיגֵּל בַּזֶּבַח נִתְפַּגֵּל הַשְּׁלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts by adding to the משנה's fetus case, explaining what happens in the other direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the קרבן is made פיגול, its fetus becomes פיגול. An intention about the fetus alone does not make the קרבן פיגול.

steps.title: The same one-way rule for the neck tendon and the crop
steps.stepSummary: Continuing his rule, רבי אלעזר says that if a bird is made פיגול through the אלל, the crop (מוראה) becomes פיגול too. An intention about the crop does not make the אלל פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made פיגול with the neck tendon, the crop becomes פיגול. If he did it with the crop, the neck tendon does not become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second example of the same one-way rule, this time with two parts of a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אלל can be eaten, so an intention about it can make the bird פיגול, and then the crop follows along. The crop is a weaker part that most people do not eat. So an intention about the crop cannot spread back to the אלל, just as the fetus could not spread back to the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The crop of a bird, a pouch in its throat that is not usually eaten

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's rule runs one way: the stronger part passes פיגול to the weaker part, but the weaker part never passes it back.

phrases.english: If he made פיגול with the neck tendon, the crop becomes פיגול.
With the crop, the neck tendon does not become פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second case in the same statement of רבי אלעזר, applying the one-way rule to bird parts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול intention about the אלל spreads to the crop. A פיגול intention about the crop does not spread to the אלל.

steps.title: Wrong intention about the אימורים makes the burned bulls פיגול, but not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר applies his one-way rule to the פרים הנשרפים. Wrong intention about the אימורים spreads to the bulls. Wrong intention about the bulls does not spread to the אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made it פיגול through the אימורים, the bulls become פיגול. If the wrong intention was about the bulls, the אימורים do not become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the third example of his rule, this time about the bulls whose meat is burned outside the camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אימורים go on the מזבח, so they are the main part, and a wrong intention about them pulls the bulls along. The bulls' meat is not eaten and not put on the מזבח, so a wrong intention about it does nothing. It is the same one-way pattern as the fetus in step 26 and the crop in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats and inner parts that are burned on the מזבח
Bulls whose meat is burned outside the camp instead of being eaten

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's rule only goes one way. A wrong intention about the main part spreads to the attached part, never the other way: from the קרבן to the fetus, from the אלל to the crop, and from the אימורים to the bulls.

phrases.english: If he made it פיגול through the sacrificial portions, the bulls become פיגול.
phrases.notes: This is still רבי אלעזר speaking. The bulls here are the ones whose meat is burned outside, not eaten.

phrases.english: Through the bulls, the sacrificial portions do not become פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third application of רבי אלעזר's one-way rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrong intention about the אימורים of the burned bulls makes the bulls פיגול. A wrong intention about the bulls does not make the אימורים פיגול.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to support רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: even those who hold that פיגול applies to the burned bulls agree that an intention about eating or burning the bulls themselves does nothing. It then asks whether this implies that an intention about the אימורים does make the bulls פיגול, as רבי אלעזר says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a source supports him: 'And they agree that if he intended about eating the bulls or burning them, he did nothing at all.' Does this not mean that if he intended about the אימורים, the bulls do become פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and reads a hidden implication out of it to back up רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only that an intention about the bulls themselves does nothing. The גמרא reasons that because the ברייתא limits its 'nothing' to the bulls, an intention about the אימורים must work and make the bulls פיגול. That is exactly רבי אלעזר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him
He did nothing at all; the intention has no effect
Is it not so that...? Used to pull an implication out of a source

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
And they agree that if he intended
phrases.notes: 'They' means even the תנאים who hold that פיגול can apply to these burned bulls.

phrases.english: about eating the bulls or burning them,
he did nothing at all.
What, does it not mean that if he intended about the sacrificial portions,
the bulls become פיגול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to back up the ruling in step 28 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule that a wrong intention about the אימורים makes the burned bulls פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that says an intention about eating or burning the bulls does nothing, which seems to imply that an intention about the אימורים does work

steps.title: The גמרא begins to reject the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers 'No' and starts to reject the suggested reading of the ברייתא. The explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to the proof. This opens a rejection, and the reason is given in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'No' means the ברייתא does not have to be read the way step 29 suggested. The גמרא is about to offer another way to understand the ברייתא, one that does not support רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: No; this introduces a rejection of the suggested proof

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished off yet. The 'No' only starts the rejection, and the actual reason comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: No;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 29
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from the ברייתא in step 29
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated. The ברייתא can be read in a way that does not support רבי אלעזר, and the reason continues in the next lines.
